By way of present judgment, this court shall conscientiously ad-
judicate upon suit for recovery of Rs.10,60,000/- (Rs. Ten Lakhs Abdul Wahid vs. Mohd. Shahid
and Sixty Thousand Only) along with interest @ 18% p.a. filed by the plaintiff against the defendant.
Case Of The Plaintiff As Per Plaint 2

Succinctly, the necessary facts for just adjudication of the present suit, as stated in the plaint, are as under:-
(i). That the Plaintiff is a law abiding and peace loving citizen of India.

(ii). That the defendant represented to the Plaintiff that he is the ab- solute owner and in possession of a Flat under construction, sit- uated on the Ground Floor, without Roof Rights (Two Room Set & One Shop Size 7'X8'), Land area measuring 50 Sq. Yds., in the Property bearing No. 52A, out of Khasra No.3, in the area of Village Wazirabad, abadi known as Sangam Vihar, Gali No.3, Delhi-110084.

(iii). That the defendant entered into an Agreement with the plain- tiff on 15.11.2018 for sale of his property under construction i.e. "Flat situated on the Ground Floor, without Roof Rights (Two Room Set & One Shop Size 7'x8'), Land area measuring 50 Sq. Yds., in the Property bearing No.
52A, out of Khasra No.3, in the area of Village Wazirabad, abadi known as Sangam Vihar, Gali No.3,
Delhi- 110084 with common passage & stairs lead- ing from ground floor to roof of the property with water tank & Dish T.V. to be put on Mumty/roof of the top floor, as well as usage of all the common facilities in the aforesaid "building"
Abdul Wahid vs. Mohd. Shahid for total sale consideration of 9,30,000/- (Nine lacs thirty thou- sand only).

That out of total sale consideration of 9,30,000/- ( Nine lacs thirty thousand only), the plaintiff paid a sum of 6,30,000/- (Six lacs thirty thousand only) to the defendant as earnest money/Bayana on 15.11.2018 at the time of execution of afore- said Agreement.

The balance sale consideration of Rs.3,00,000/- (Three lacs only) was payable by the plaintiff to the defendant on or before 15.02.2019 at the time of execution and registration of proper transfer documents/Sale Deed in favour of the plaintiff or his nominees at his (Plaintiff's) option.

(v). That before execution of Agreement dated 15.11.2018, the de- fendant had assured the plaintiff that the proposed property/Flat under sale is free from all sorts of encumbrances such as sale,
mortgage, gift, transfer, lien, decree, security, surety, burden charges, dispute, notifications, court injunctions, acquisition, complications, attachments, notices, wills, legal flaws etc. and that there is no legal defect in the title of the defendant regard- ing his ownership and that the defendant was fully empowered and competent to sell and transfer the said property in question unto the plaintiff by way of sale deed or other transfer docu- ments.

(vi). That it was one of the conditions in the Agreement dated 15.11.2018 that if the defendant fails to execute the sale deed and/or proper transfer documents of the said property in favour of the plaintiff within the stipulated period then he would be li- Abdul Wahid vs. Mohd. Shahid able to pay double the amount of earnest money to the plaintiff and similarly, if the plaintiff fails to make payment of the bal- ance amount to the defendant within stipulated period, then his earnest money would be treated as forfeited.
(vii).That the plaintiff had entered into above said Agreement dated 15.11.2018 with the defendant basically on his assurances as contained in the same.

The defendant had also assured the plaintiff that he would positively show and supply a copy each of the previous documents of the property under sale to the plaintiff within 1 month from 15.11.2018 on the pretext that the same were lying in his home town.

The defendant also assured the plaintiff and it is also one of the terms of the agreement that all the previous original documents would be handed over to the plaintiff at the time of execution of Sale Deed or proper transfer documents.

(viii). That it was also agreed between the defendant and the plain- tiff that all kinds of dues in respect of the property under sale upto the date of execution of the sale Deed and/or proper trans- fer documents, would be paid by the defendant.

(ix). That after execution of Agreement dated 15.11.2018, the plaintiff kept on requesting the defendant to give a copy each of the previous title documents of the said property and complete the construction of the said Flat so as to enable him (the Plain- tiff) to shift into the same.
However, the defendant kept putting off on one pretext or the other.
Abdul Wahid vs. Mohd. Shahid (x).

That surprisingly, even on the stipulated date of execution of Sale Deed and/or proper transfer documents i.e. 15.02.2019, the defendant had not started the construction of the proposed flat and Abdul Wahid vs . Mohd. Shahid on 6 May, 2023

2 was not in a position to transfer the non-existent Flat in favour of the plaintiff.

Therefore, the defendant became liable to pay double the amount of the earnest money of 6,30,000/- (Six lacs thirty thousand only) to the plaintiff which comes to 12,60,000/- (Twelve lacs sixty thousand only).
The defendant however, promised to immediately start the construction of the Flat but in vain.
The defendant neither started the construction of the Flat nor paid double the amount of earnest money to the plaintiff.

(xi). That after repeated requests and demands, on 01.03.2019, the defendant requested the plaintiff to extend the date of execution of Sale Deed for another three months, upto 30.05.2019 to which the plaintiff agreed.

The defendant also promised to pro- vide a rented 'two room set' accommodation to the plaintiff at his (defendant's) cost and expenses, till the construction of the Flat under sale was completed i.e. 30.05.2019.
The defendant also promised to pay double the amount of earnest money, if the construction of the said Flat was not completed till the extended date of 31.05.2019.
Aforesaid terms were reduced into writing on 01.03.2019 on the back of the first page of the Agreement dated 15.11.2018 and signed by both the parties.
The defendant however, did not provide the promised 'rented two room set' ac- Abdul Wahid vs. Mohd. Shahid commodation to the plaintiff and kept on passing time on one pretext or the other.

sentences.text: (xii). That after a few days the defendant again showed his inabil- ity in starting the construction of the said Flat.

On 22.04.2019 the defendant threatened the plaintiff to either accept a lump sum amount of 7,50,000/- ( Seven lacs fifty thousand only) or forget the amount paid by the plaintiff to the defendant as earnest money at the time of execution of the Agreement dated 18.11.2018.
(xiii).
That seeing no other alternative, the plaintiff agreed to ac- cept the proposal of the defendant.

The defendant paid a sum of 2,00,000/- (Two lacs only) to the plaintiff on 22.04.2019 in cash and promised to shortly pay the balance of the settled amount of 5,50,000/- (Five lacs fifty thousand only).
The acknowledge- ment of receipt of Rs.2,00,000/- (Rs Two lacs only) has been acknowledged by the Plaintiff on the backside of the first page of the Agreement dated 15.11.2018.
(xiv).

That after repeated requests and demands of the balance set- tled amount of Rs. 5,50,000/-
(Five thousand five hundred only) by the Plaintiff, the defendant got issued a Post-dated Cheque on 17.07.2019, from the Bank account of his wife namely Mrs. Rukhsana, bearing cheque No.000955 dated 24.07.2019 for Rs.5,50,000/- (Five thousand five hundred only), favouring the plaintiff,
drawn on ICICI Bank, 112, Block T, Dayanand Road, Daryaganj, Delhi-110002 alongwith Covering Letter dated 17.07.2019, with the assurance that the same was good for pay- Abdul Wahid vs. Mohd. That however, before the plaintiff could deposit aforesaid cheque in his Bank account on the stipulated date, the defendant requested him not to do so on the pretext that the amount, which was expected to be credited in the bank account of his wife for encashment of the cheque bearing Abdul Wahid vs . 3 No.000955, was not received and that therefore, the said cheque would not be hon- oured if deposited.
The defendant promised to shortly give an- other date to the plaintiff for deposit of the said cheque in Bank within its validity but in vain.

(xvi). That thereafter, the defendant had been repeatedly promising the plaintiff from time to time to shortly give a date for deposit of the cheque in Bank or in the alternative to pay cash but of no avail.
In the meanwhile the validity of the Cheque has even ex- pired and resultantly, the terms of the agreement/ settlement, as detailed in foregoing para No.13, have been breached by the de- fendant

and he has now become liable to pay a sum of Rs.10,60,000/- (Ten lacs sixty thousand only)
to the plaintiff i.e. Rs. 12,60,000/- (double of earnest money), less Rs.2,00,000/- paid by the defendant to the Plaintiff on 22.04.2019.
After this, the defendant has been gaining time by making promises and promises only, but of no avail.

Since the amount payable by the defendant to the plaintiff's long overdue, he is also liable to pay Abdul Wahid vs. Mohd. Shahid interest @ 18% per annum to the plaintiff from 15.11.2018 till the date of realization.

sentences.text: (xvii). That the defendant had dishonest and fraudulent intention from the very beginning in execution of which he lured and in- duced the plaintiff to enter into aforesaid Agreement dated 15.11.2018 and to part with his hard earned money amounting to 6,30,000/- ( Six lacs thirty thousand only) as earnest money with clear intent not to construct the proposed Flat till the stipu- lated date and not to honour other terms of the said Agreement and to not deliver the possession of the residential Flat with col- lusion and connivance of his wife, namely Mrs. Rukhsana, so as to cheat and defraud him.

the plaintiff has now learnt that the defendant was even not the owner of the plot of land on which the Flat under Agreement was proposed to be constructed and had no right,
title or authority to enter into Agreement dated 15.11.2018.
Therefore, the defendant and his wife are also li- able to be prosecuted under Sections 420/406/120B/34 IPC. (xviii).

That now a sum of Rs.10,60,000/- ( Ten lacs sixty thousand only) is due and recoverable by the Plaintiff from the defendant, which has not been paid by him despite repeated requests and demands with malafide intention so as to cheat and harass the Plaintiff.
(xix).
That since the aforesaid amount is long overdue, the defen- dant is also liable to pay interest to the Plaintiff @ 18% per an- num from 22.04.2019, till the date of realisation.
Abdul Wahid vs. Mohd. Shahid (xx).

That since the defendant has been avoiding to perform his part of the contract as stated hereinabove elsewhere, the Plain- tiff has got issued a legal Notice dated 05.09.2020 to the defen- dant, through Advocate by Speed Post and Courier, thereby calling upon him to pay a sum of Rs.10,60,000/- (Ten lacs sixty thousand only) to the plaintiff along with interest @ 18% per annum within 7 days from the date of receipt of Notice, failing which to file a suit against him for recovery with damages and costs.
The defendant was further called upon to pay a sum of Rs.21,000/- ( Twenty one thousand only) as the charges of legal notice.
The notice has been duly served upon the defendant but despite service of notice, he has failed to reply or comply with the same.
3 Summons for settlement of issues were issued to the defendant, who appeared before the court and filed Written Statement along with affidavit of truth.

CASE OF DEFENDANT AS PER WRITTEN STATEMENT 4

Succinctly, the case of defendants is as under:
(i) That the plaintiff has filed a false, concocted and merit less suit and the same is liable to be dismissed at outset.
The documents and affidavit filed along with the plaint are wrong, vexatious and vehemently denied and any reference to them by the plaintiff is incorrect and untenable.

Further, the plaintiff has not Abdul Wahid vs.
Mohd. Shahid approached this court with clean hands and the plaintiff has deliberately concealed, misrepresented and suppressed various material facts and circumstances from this court and on this ground alone the present suit is liable to be dismissed in limine.

The defendant reserve the right to initiate proceedings against the plaintiff for initiating such false and frivolous proceedings against the defendant based on wrong and baseless allegations and on false affidavits and assertions which are contrary to the facts and circumstances of the present case.
(ii). That the present suit filed by the Plaintiff is not maintainable either on law or on facts of the present case.
The Plaintiff has filed the present suit without any basis.
The present suit is meritless and is also an abuse of the due process of law and hence the same is liable to be dismissed with exemplary costs in favor of the Defendant and against the Plaintiff.

(iii) That at the outset the responding Defendant denied each and every allegation made in the Plaint, which is not otherwise admitted hereunder, as being false,
frivolous and baseless.
The suit is preposterous and is a gross abuse of the process of law and is liable to be dismissed.
(iv). That the present suit is liable to be dismissed as there is no cause of action in favour of Plaintiff and Abdul Wahid vs. Mohd. Shahid against the answering Defendant.

In fact the plaintiff has not complied with the terms and conditions of the agreement dated 15/11/2018 executed between the parties to this suit wherein the time was the essence of the said agreement and the plaintiff failed to pay the balance consideration amount within the time limitation thus after lapse of the time the plaintiff left no right to agitate upon the aforesaid agreement.
(v) That the present suit is not maintainable as the Plaintiff has concocted a false story in the Plaint.

It is submitted that the Plaintiff has not filed the plaint according to the commercial courts act, which requires every page of the pleading to be signed and attested without which it has to be taken that the plaint is having without any cause of action and is liable to be rejected outrightedly.
(vi). That the present suit filed by the Plaintiff herein is liable to be rejected under Order 7 Rule 11 of Code of Civil Procedure, 1908.

It is stated that the facts averred by the Plaintiff are false, and are stated in order to create a moonshine cause of action,
hence the present suit is liable to be rejected.

Abdul Wahid vs . Mohd. Shahid on 6 May, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/30063437/
5 (vii).
That the Plaintiff's present suit is not maintainable as the same does not have a locus standi to file the present Suit.
Abdul Wahid vs. Mohd. Shahid (viii).
That the present suit is liable to be dismissed as the Plaintiff has filed the present suit simply to harass and humiliate the Defendant.
(ix). That the present suit of the Plaintiff is nothing else but a way to harass the Defendant to implicate him in false and frivolous cases.
The entire story as made out by the Plaintiff in the Plaint is nothing but the outcome of malicious and misconceived acts of the Plaintiff.
The entire story put forth by the Plaintiff is cooked up and concocted one and thus the suit of the Plaintiff is liable to be dismissed with heavy and exemplary costs.
(x) The Plaintiff has filed the present false and frivolous suit on the basis of distorted facts so as to file and maintain the present suit.
So, the suit of the Plaintiff is liable to be dismissed solely on this ground alone.
(xi). That the suit of the plaintiff is also not maintainable and is liable to be dismissed.
The plaintiff is not entitled to get the relief as prayed for in the plaint.
REPLICATION 5
Plaintiff filed the Replication controverting the allegations/ contentions in the Written Statement of the Defendant and contents of the plaint have been reiterated and reaffirmed.
Abdul Wahid vs. Mohd. Shahid EX-PARTE PROCEEDINGS 6
Thereafter, defendant stopped appearing before the court and accordingly, the defendant was proceeded ex-parte vide Order dated 02/02/2023.
PLAINTIFF'S EVIDENCE 7
The plaintiff, in order to prove his case, has led plaintiff evi- dence and got examined himself as PW-1.
PW-1 has filed his evi- dence by way of affidavit, wherein he reiterated and reaffirmed the contents of the plaint.

PW-1 in his testimony has relied upon the following documents:-
i. Legal notice dated 05/09/2020 is ExPW1/1.
ii. Original postal receipt of speed post dated 05/09/2020 is ExPW1/2.

iii. Original receipt dated 05/09/2020 of the professional couriers  is ExPW1/3.
 iv.
Tracking report of speed post is ExPW1/4.

v. Tracking report of courier is ExPW1/5.
 vi.

Original agreement to sell dated 15/11/2018 is ExPW1/6.
 vii.
Cash receipt dated 15/11/2018 for Rs.6,30,000/- is ExPW1/7.
viii. Original cheque baring no. 000955 dated 24/07/2019 for Rs.5,50,000/- is ExPW1/8.

6 ix.
Covering letter dated 17/07/2019 is ExPW1/9. x.

Certificate u/s 65B of Indian Evidence Act regarding tracking Abdul Wahid vs. Mohd. Shahid report of speed post and courier is ExPW1/10.
8
No final arguments have been advanced on behalf of plaintiff.
I have perused the material available on record.
FINDINGS OF THE COURT 9

The plaintiff has filed the present suit for recovery of Rs.10,60,000/-
against the defendant.
The present suit of the plain- tiff is well within the period of limitation.

In the present case, the defendant was proceeded ex-parte, despite this fact, the plaintiff has to prove his case on merits and satisfy the Court that the plain- tiff is entitled to the recovery of Rs.10,60,000/-
and interest @ 18% per annum .
10 In the present case, defendant has not cross-examined the PW- 1 to contradict or disprove the case of the plaintiff.

When the de- fendant has chosen not to appear and when the case of the plaintiff has gone un-challenged, un-controverted, un-rebutted and duly corroborated by the documents, this Court has no reason to disbe- lieve the version of the plaintiff.
11 The present suit of the plaintiff is well within the period of lim- itation.
In the present case, the PW-1 has proved on record the doc- uments, as mentioned in his testimony, showing the liability of the defendant to pay the suit amount alongwith interest to the plaintiff.
The plaintiff has been able to prove his case.

On the other hand Abdul Wahid vs. Mohd.
Shahid defendant though had mentioned legal notice and postal receipt in his written statement,
however none of these documents were ever brought on record.
Defendant has also contended that time was the essence of the contract, however, no document has been brought on record in support of the contention.
Hence, the suit of the plaintiff is entitled to be decreed.
However, the plaintiff has sought recovery of Rs. 10,60,000/- alongwith interest @ 18% per annum.
Plaintiff in the present case had paid an amount of Rs. 6,30,000/- to the defendant as earnest money, out of which, Rs. 2 Lakhs was refunded by the defendant to the plaintiff on 22.04.2019.

Plaintiff is claiming double of the amount of the earnest money as per clause (3) of the agreement to sell dated 15.11.2018 Ex.PW1/6.
12

The Hon'ble Supreme Court in ONGC Ltd. v. Saw Pipes Ltd., (2003) 5 SCC 705 held as under:-
"64. .... Section 74 emphasizes that in case of breach of contract, the party complaining of the breach is entitled to receive reasonable compensation whether or not actual loss is proved to have been caused by such breach.

entities.text: ONGC Ltd. v. Saw Pipes Ltd., (2003) 5 SCC 705
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Therefore, the emphasis is on reasonable compensation.
If the compensation named in the contract is by way of penalty, consideration would be different and the party is only entitled to reasonable compensation for the loss suffered.

But if the compensation named in the contract for such breach is genuine preestimate of loss which the parties knew when they made the contract to be likely to result from the breach of it, there is no question Abdul Wahid vs . Mohd. Shahid on 6 May, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/30063437/
7 of proving such loss or such party is not required to lead evidence to prove actual loss suffered by him.
Burden is on the other party to lead evidence for proving that no loss is likely to occur by such breach...."
Abdul Wahid vs. Mohd. Shahid
In clause 3 of the Ex.PW1/6, the compesation is by way of penalty and thus the plaintiff is entitled to reasonable compensation for the loss suffered by him.
Plaintiff has paid an amount of Rs. 6,30,000/- out of which Rs. 2 Lakhs has already been returned by the defendant.
Thus, the plaintiff is entitled to Rs. 4,30,000/- from the defendant.
Plaintiff has also sought interest @ 18% per annum from 22/04/2019 till the date of its realisation.

The court is of the considered opinion that the interest of justice would be served if the plaitniff is granted interest @
12% per annum from 22/04/2019 till its realisation.
13 Applying priori and posteriori reasoning, this court held that plaintiff has been able to prove her case against the defendant.
RELIEF

From the discussions, as adumbrated hereinabove, I hereby pass the following FINAL ORDER (a) a decree of Rs.4.30 lakhs (Rupees Four Lakhs Thirty Thou- sand only) is passed in favour of the plaintiff and against the defendants alongwith simple interest @ 12% per annum from 22/04/2019 till its realisation.
(b) The cost of the suit is also awarded in favour of the plaintiff and against the defendants.
Abdul Wahid vs. Mohd. Shahid Decree-sheet be prepared accordingly.
